decisions.reason: The client explicitly states that the Hero V's refined right-arm termination will shape the smaller V, adding a required terminal derivation to its shared geometry.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
I genuinely feel that something fundamental shifted after our last conversation. When we stopped discussing what the V should look like and began focusing on who it represents, it felt as though we finally started designing from the same sense of purpose. Thank you for asking such insightful questions. The philosophy is clearly present in this round, and I appreciate the care with which you translated it.

Option 2 is my favorite.

Honestly, I’m wondering whether this could be the V. It feels more complete than everything else we've explored so far.

The one remaining refinement I’d like to investigate is the very end of the right arm. When my eye follows the gesture upward, I want it to conclude with full conviction instead of slowly fading away. Not longer. Not thicker. Not more curved. Simply a slightly more intentional finish, as though it knows precisely where it is going.

I also realized that this termination will define more than the large V; it will eventually shape the smaller V and, even more importantly, the É accent. Since this gesture will become one of the Vellvé identity's defining signatures, I think it is worth considering whether it communicates the same quiet confidence and sense of becoming that the brand embodies.

value_updates.terminal_derivation: The smaller V must be shaped by the Hero V's right-arm termination gesture, including its intentional and confident finish.

decisions.reason: The client explicitly states that the Hero V's refined right-arm termination will shape the É accent and become a defining identity signature.

decisions.reason: The source changes the Hero V termination and explicitly identifies only the smaller V and É accent as derivative forms; it does not change the deferred E and L letterform requirements.
The client's appreciation of the design discussion does not change the standing requirement to provide rationale with each design round.
The word 'finish' describes the geometric termination of the Hero V's right arm, not the deferred champagne-metal material treatment.
The source refines the Hero V's geometry and its derivation into the smaller V and É accent but does not change wordmark spacing or kerning.
The selection of a design option and refinement of its right-arm termination do not affect accepted review-image formats or file accessibility.
